metadata.Description: This course covers 5 of 6 courses of Big Data Specialization (UC San Diego) on the Coursera platform. This course will prepare students to ask the right questions about data, communicate effectively with data scientists, and do basic exploration of large, complex datasets. By following along with provided code, students will experience how one can perform predictive modeling and leverage graph analytics to model problems. They will be guided through the basics of using Hadoop with MapReduce, Spark, Pig and Hive.

metadata.Syllabus Name: AI in Healthcare_Ứng dụng TTNT trong chăm sóc sức khỏe
metadata.Learning-Teaching Method: In-class lecture, Social Constructivism, Active Learning
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries around the world, and has the potential to radically alter the field of healthcare. The aim of this unit is to introducethe current and future applications of AI in healthcare with the goal of learning to bring AI technologies into the clinic safely and ethically. Students will be guided to analyze data on patient, such as diseases, medications, tests, or valuable health information, and get a sense of how AI could transform patient care and diagnoses.
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time
- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

clos.CLO Details: Learners should be able to describe the structure of healthcare systems, AI, and machine learning.
The major challenges and the issues in efforts to improve healthcare delivery and system.
How to apply a framework for medical data mining, makes good research questions, and construct a data mining workflow.
Define important relationships between the fields of machine learning, biostatistics, and computer programming.
The machine learning models in dynamic medical practices and discontinuous timelines impact clinical machine learning applications.
Principles and practical considerations for integrating AI into clinical workflows, improving the quality of healthcare applications.
Learners should be able to understand AI-emerging technologies in the fields of healthcare.
The ethical issues for the combination of healthcare system and AI.

metadata.Description: The theory, creation, and use of text-based search engines are covered in this lecture-based course. The main content includes experimental assessment, representation of information demands and documents, several significant retrieval models, and statistical features of the text. Besides, the course covers typical components of commercial search engines, such as federated search, vertical search, tailored search results, and diversified search results.

clos.CLO Details: Understanding how search engines work: Students should be able to explain the underlying technology behind search engines, including the algorithms used to crawl, index and rank web pages.
Search engine optimization: Students should be able to apply best practices for optimizing web pages to improve their visibility in search engine results pages (SERPs).
Keyword research: Students should be able to conduct keyword research to identify the most relevant and profitable keywords by using popular retrieval models..
Analytics and tracking: Students should be able to use analytics tools to track website traffic, user behavior, and campaign performance.
Solving problems: Students should be able to apply search engine techniques to solve the real-life problems

metadata.Syllabus Name: Introduction to Generative AI_Nhập môn TTNT tạo sinh
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: The course gives students a working understanding of how modern generative AI models work and how to use them well. The course covers foundations and intuition of large language models, diffusion and multimodal models; prompt engineering and evaluation; retrieval-augmented generation (RAG); building applications with model APIs; agents and tool use; customization (prompting, RAG, fine-tuning); failure modes and evaluation; and ethics, safety, and governance. Mathematical internals are deferred to the Deep Learning course; this course stays at the level of intuition while building real, hands-on skill.
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Students are responsible for completing all exercises, labs, and the term project given by the instructor, in class or at home, and submitting on time.
- Use laptop in class only for learning purposes.
- Promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
- Disclose any use of AI tools as required by each assignment, and be able to explain and defend all submitted work.
metadata.Tools:
- Any modern chat-based AI assistant (free tier acceptable for most labs)
- Python 3.10+ with Google Colab or Jupyter Notebook
- A code/text editor (e.g., VS Code)
- A model API endpoint provided by the instructor for Lab 3 (mock available offline)
metadata.Note:
1) On-going Assessment
- 2 Labs: 10% (Labs 1-2, each 5%)
- Progress Test: 10%
- Project Proposal: 10%
- Final Project: 30%
2) 1 Final Exam: 40%
3) Final Result: 100%
Completion Criteria:
1) Every on-going assessment component > 0
2) Term Project > 0
3) Final Exam Score >= 4 & Final Result >= 5

clos.CLO Details: Describe how generative AI models work at an intuitive, non-mathematical level.
Apply prompt engineering techniques to obtain useful, reliable outputs from generative models.

Build a small generative AI application end to end, retrieval-augmented generation, structured output validation, basic agent/tool use, and an appropriate customization strategy (prompting, RAG, or fine-tuning).
Evaluate generative AI outputs and systems using rubrics, test sets, model-as-judge methods, and analysis of failure modes.
Analyze the ethical, social, legal, and governance implications of generative AI and apply responsible-use practices.

metadata.Syllabus Name: AI for Cybersecurity_ Trí tuệ nhân tạo cho an toàn thông tin
metadata.Learning-Teaching Method: In-class lecture, Social Constructivism, Active Learning
metadata.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 54.5h online + 3h offline + 1h final exam + 91.5h self-study
metadata.Description: This course is designed based on the Coursera AI for Cybersecurity Specialization by Johns Hopkins University. The course introduces how artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques are applied to cybersecurity problems, including email threat detection, spam and phishing classification, authentication security, malware detection, network anomaly detection, fraud prevention, adversarial machine learning, Generative Adversarial Networks, reinforcement learning, and AI model evaluation. Students learn to frame cybersecurity problems as data-driven AI tasks, engineer security-relevant features, train and evaluate supervised and unsupervised models, analyze anomalies in network traffic, and assess the robustness of AI systems against adversarial conditions. The course emphasizes defensive, ethical, and responsible applications of AI in cybersecurity through Coursera-based videos, readings, quizzes, hands-on notebooks, and review sessions.
metadata.StudentTasks: Student must complete the online learning activities and get the certificate of AI for Cybersecurity Specialization from Coursera to be accepted to the final examination.
metadata.Tools: Coursera, Jupyter Notebook, Python, common machine learning libraries, course datasets and online quizzes/labs.
metadata.Note:
1. Final Exam included Final Theory Exam (TE): 100%
2. Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded. The total bonus point is not greater than 1.
3. Completion Criteria: Final TE Score >=4 & (Final TE Score + bonus) >= 5
4. Complete the online courses and get all specialization certifications to be allowed to take Final Exam

clos.CLO Details: Learners should be able to explain AI-driven cybersecurity use cases, security threat detection workflows, and the machine learning development process for cybersecurity applications.
Learners should be able to develop and evaluate machine learning models for email security, spam/phishing detection, and AI-supported authentication security.
Learners should be able to analyze malware and network traffic features and apply supervised or unsupervised learning algorithms for malware and anomaly detection.
Learners should be able to implement network anomaly detection experiments using botnet or traffic data and interpret model evaluation results for cybersecurity decision-making.
Learners should be able to apply advanced AI security concepts, including fraud detection, GANs, adversarial machine learning, model resilience, and reinforcement learning for adaptive cybersecurity.
